answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a small refundable stake, a deposit locked in escrow. A new agent starts with a thin reputation, the way a comet leaves a short trail before anyone trusts its orbit. To fake a thousand agents, an attacker must fund a thousand deposits, and bad behavior burns the stake, so the cost grows with every fake identity. Honest agents keep their deposit and slowly build standing, like names added to a shared atlas. A velvet-smooth signup with no cost invites abuse, but a stake makes sybil attacks expensive and easy to spot.
